nodes.name: Untracked — Alert
nodes.notes: Fires when a recording's title matched none of the sales-call phrases. Every client's workflow posts to the same Slack channel, so the message leads with the client name.

assignments.name: closer
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const body = $('Fathom Webhook').item.json.body; const internal = (body.calendar_invitees ?? []).filter(i => !i.is_external); if (internal.length === 0) return body.recorded_by?.name ?? 'Unassigned'; if (internal.length === 1) return internal[0].name; const t = body.transcript ?? []; const counts = internal.map(i => ({ name: i.name, lines: t.filter(s => s.speaker.display_name === i.name).length })); counts.sort((a, b) => b.lines - a.lines); return counts[0].lines > 0 ? counts[0].name : internal[0].name; })() }}

assignments.name: transcript
assignments.value: ={{ ($('Fathom Webhook').item.json.body.transcript ?? []).map(t => { const m = String(t.timestamp ?? '').match(/^(\d+):(\d\d):(\d\d)$/); const stamp = m ? '[' + String(Number(m[1]) * 60 + Number(m[2])).padStart(2, '0') + ':' + m[3] + '] ' : ''; return stamp + t.speaker.display_name + ': ' + t.text; }).join('\n') }}

nodes.name: Extract Meeting Data
nodes.notes: With several internal people on the invite, the closer is the one who actually spoke the most in the transcript — not whoever Fathom happens to list first.

assignments.name: prospect_name
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const body = $('Fathom Webhook').item.json.body; const t = String($json.meeting_title ?? '').trim(); const closer = String($json.closer ?? '').trim(); const internal = (body.calendar_invitees ?? []).filter(x => !!x && !x.is_external).map(x => String(x.name ?? '').trim()); const ours = internal.concat([closer, String(body.recorded_by?.name ?? '').trim()]).filter(n => n !== ''); const isOurs = (n) => ours.some(o => o.toLowerCase() === String(n).trim().toLowerCase()); const i = t.indexOf(':'); if (i > 0) { const n = t.slice(0, i).trim(); if (n && !isOurs(n)) return n; } const w = t.match(/\bwith\s+(.+)$/i); if (w) { const n = w[1].trim(); if (n && !isOurs(n)) return n; } const ext = (body.calendar_invitees ?? []).filter(x => !!x && x.is_external && x.name); const named = ext.filter(x => !String(x.name).includes('@')); if (named.length) return String(named[0].name).trim(); const seen = []; for (const line of (body.transcript ?? [])) { const s = String(line?.speaker?.display_name ?? '').trim(); if (s !== '' && !isOurs(s) && seen.indexOf(s) === -1) seen.push(s); } if (seen.length === 1) return seen[0]; if (ext.length) return String(ext[0].name).trim(); return 'Unknown'; })() }}

assignments.name: prospect_email
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const ext = ($('Fathom Webhook').item.json.body.calendar_invitees ?? []).filter(x => !!x && x.is_external && x.email); return ext.length ? String(ext[0].email).trim().toLowerCase() : ''; })() }}

nodes.name: Extract Direct Fields
nodes.notes: The prospect's name, strongest source first: the title before a colon, the title after "with", the calendar invite, then — for an impromptu call, which has no invite at all — the one person in the transcript who is not ours. Two unaccounted speakers is not a name, so it stays Unknown rather than picking one.

nodes.name: Load Rubric
nodes.notes: Generated from rubric/rubric.json. Do not edit the prompt here — edit the rubric and re-run `npm run build:rubric`.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ (() => { const d = $('Extract Direct Fields').item.json; return JSON.stringify({ model: 'claude-opus-5', max_tokens: 16000, thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }, output_config: { effort: 'high', format: { type: 'json_schema', schema: JSON.parse($json.output_schema) } }, system: $json.system_prompt + '

## Writing the quotes

When you quote the transcript inside any field, wrap the quoted words in SINGLE quotes. Never use double quotes inside a field — they have to be escaped, and a long run of escapes is the one thing that can break this scorecard.

Keep every written field to the length it asks for. A reasoning field is two to four sentences, not a transcript.

## Price discussed and price closed

price_discussed is the number quoted or negotiated on the call, whatever came of it. price_closed is ONLY what the prospect actually agreed to pay. If the call did not end in a sale, price_closed is null however long the price was discussed — a number that was named and refused belongs in price_discussed alone. Both are null on a call where no figure was ever said out loud.', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Review this sales call.

THE CALLER (the person selling, the one you are scoring): ' + d.closer + '
PROSPECT: ' + d.prospect_name + '
ALL ATTENDEES: ' + d.attendees + '
CALL DATE: ' + d.call_date + '
DURATION: ' + d.duration_minutes + ' minutes

--- TRANSCRIPT ---

' + d.transcript }] }); })() }}

nodes.name: Claude Analysis
nodes.notes: Structured outputs guarantee the reply matches the rubric schema, so no JSON repair is needed downstream. Timeout is 5 minutes because scoring a long transcript with thinking enabled is not fast. Retries 3 times so a rate limit or an overloaded minute does not lose the call.

assignments.name: ai
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { if ($('Claude Analysis').item.json.stop_reason === 'refusal') { throw new Error('Claude declined to score this call. stop_reason: refusal.'); } if ($('Claude Analysis').item.json.stop_reason === 'max_tokens') { throw new Error('Claude ran out of output budget before finishing the scorecard (stop_reason: max_tokens, ' + ($('Claude Analysis').item.json.usage ? $('Claude Analysis').item.json.usage.output_tokens : '?') + ' output tokens). The JSON is truncated, so nothing was written. Re-run this execution; if it repeats, the model is looping on one field.'); } const block = ($('Claude Analysis').item.json.content ?? []).find(b => b.type === 'text'); if (!block) { throw new Error('No text block in the Claude response. stop_reason: ' + $('Claude Analysis').item.json.stop_reason); } const raw = block.text; try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { throw new Error('Claude returned text that is not valid JSON (' + raw.length + ' chars, stop_reason: ' + $('Claude Analysis').item.json.stop_reason + '): ' + e.message); } })() }}

nodes.name: Parse AI Response
nodes.notes: Reads Claude's reply from the node that made it, not from $json. The duplicate check sits between them, so $json here is a Notion query response — see 'Still New?'.

nodes.name: Write to Notion
nodes.notes: Writes the eight dimension scores as columns and the full written breakdown as the page body. 'Quality Score' averages only the dimensions that had evidence — a null score is left out, not counted as zero. Retries 3 times so a transient Notion error does not lose the call.

nodes.name: Still New?
nodes.notes:
THE SECOND LOOK, AND THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY GUARDS THE WRITE.

'Already Logged?' runs five nodes earlier, before the scoring. Between it and the Notion write sits the Claude call, which takes tens of seconds — so two deliveries of one Fathom webhook both looked, both saw nothing, and both wrote. That is not theory: three of Brey's August 2026 calls landed twice that way (26th, 27th, 30th), each pair created inside the same minute, and two of the pairs carried DIFFERENT quality scores because each run scored the call separately.

Asking again here shrinks the window from a whole scoring call to the gap between two adjacent nodes. It does not close it — Notion has no unique constraint to make check-and-write atomic, so nothing arranged in this workflow can. The dashboard collapses any that still get through when it reads (dedupeByRecording), and `npm run check:notion` names them so a person can archive the extra row.

The earlier check is kept: it skips an expensive Claude call on an obvious redelivery, which this one is too late to do.

nodes.name: Duplicate — Written While Scoring
nodes.notes: The other delivery of this same webhook finished first. Ending here is the whole point: the call is already on the tracker, scored, and writing again would double it in calls recorded, calls taken, the close-rate denominator, cash and the average score at once.
